conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, I’m Dr. Lee. I’ll be your doctor during your stay. You came in today because of pain in your left calf?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it’s been hurting more since I got back from visiting my mom. It feels tight and really aches when I walk.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. And you mentioned some shortness of breath and chest discomfort at night, especially when lying down?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it’s been worse lately. I get a bit of cough and wheezing at night. But no chest pain during the day.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Given your history of a prior blood clot and recent travel, we’re concerned about a possible clot in your leg or lungs. We’ve done an ultrasound on your legs.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, okay. Did they find anything?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, the ultrasound showed a blood clot in the deep veins of your left calf. That explains the pain and swelling.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That sounds serious. Could it have traveled?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s why we ordered a CT scan of your chest. Because of your breathing symptoms, we needed to check for a pulmonary embolism.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The CT scan is back. I’m sorry to say it shows blood clots in the arteries of your right lung. That’s what’s causing your shortness of breath.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh no… is it dangerous? Are my lungs okay?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re stable right now. No strain on your heart, and your oxygen levels are good. We’re starting you on a blood thinner called Lovenox to prevent more clots.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I need to be on that forever? I’ve had a clot before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Given your history of a prior PE and now this new one, it’s likely you’ll need long-term anticoagulation. We’ll discuss that with your oncologist.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your labs look better today. Your breathing has improved, and you walked the hallway without any drop in oxygen.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. I do feel less short of breath.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll discharge you today with Lovenox injections twice a day. You’ll also keep taking your other medications, including prednisone for your GVHD.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my eye drops? I haven’t been using them regularly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, please restart Systane every hour and Restasis twice a day. Your dry eyes are part of your chronic GVHD and need consistent care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’ll try to be better about that. And my headaches?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You can continue oxycodone as needed, up to every 8 hours. But let your doctor know if they worsen.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I follow up with my oncologist?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, definitely. They’ll manage your long-term anticoagulation and GVHD. We’ve sent them all the details.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor. I feel much better knowing what’s going on.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. We’ll have the discharge papers ready soon. Keep using your medications as prescribed and call if you have chest pain or trouble breathing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just a quick check before you leave. How are you feeling?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good, really. My leg feels better, and I can breathe normally now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Excellent. Remember to inject Lovenox every 12 hours and follow up with your team. Take care.
